_comment: Domain configuration for the finance domain — the single source of truth for categories, models and the tidy rules. This domain runs LOCALLY ONLY: no Cloudflare container, no deployment gating, no schedule block. The worker on the MacBook may therefore read the file system from inside an activity (the same exception docs/BOOK.md describes for the book domain), but writing still happens only in financecli, never in a workflow. Personal paths are NOT here — they live in the gitignored shared/finance/paths.json, because this repo is public.

categories._comment: Derived from the author's own planning workbook (finanzen_privat_project55.xlsx, sheet 'Ausgaben', measured 2026-09-24), NOT invented here. Each entry names the rows it stands for so the mapping stays checkable. 'source': 'project55' means the category exists as a line in his sheet; 'cross_cut' means it runs across several of his rows and exists because he asked to see it separately.

transfer.label: Umbuchung
transfer.note: Between his own accounts — never counts towards any spending total.

boat.label: Telsche
boat.note: Cuts across several of his rows; his own Telsche_Ausgaben.xlsx is the touchstone.

ai_stack.label: KI-Setup
ai_stack.note: The PRIVATE share only. Part of it runs on the company credit card and is deliberately absent here — the report says so rather than implying a complete figure.

library._comment: The summaries are a goal of this domain, not a by-product: without them Vibe has no context and the conversation is worthless. Three documents, no more. finance-overview.md carries NO transaction at all — it is pure planning context out of Project 55 and therefore the harmless one that makes Vibe useful first. Set enabled to false and everything stays on the machine; the local conversational workflow and the generated workbook keep working.
library.name: Portfolio Strategie Bibliothek
library._id_comment: His existing library, not a new one. It already holds anlagestrategie.md (23.07.2026, 30k characters: target figure, crash rules, regime-change signals, override protocol). Putting the summaries next to the rulebook is what makes Vibe able to answer a question about a booking AND about what the rules say to do. A second library would have split the context in half.

tidy._comment: Phase 0: one place for everything private-financial. The rules are data, not code, so a wrong target is a JSON edit rather than a patch. Preview is the default; every move is logged to workflows/data/finance/moves.jsonl and reversible. Nothing is renamed, nothing merged, no sub-structure flattened.
tidy._accounts_comment: Statement files are sorted into Konten/<account> by what their file name starts with. The prefixes are IBAN fragments and card names, so the map itself lives in the gitignored shared/finance/paths.json under accounts_from_filename — not here.

out_of_scope._comment: Folder names that are WORK material and must never enter the private ledger — these are receipts for the company credit card. Only the names live here; where they should go is a personal path and therefore sits in shared/finance/paths.json under out_of_scope_targets.

tidy._scatter_comment: A holding pen, deliberately not Belege/. The patterns match a FILE NAME and nothing has looked inside — and the first real preview (2026-09-24) showed why that matters: 54 of 57 hits were work material (vendor invoices, company-card summaries), not private. Collecting them into one place is still worth it, because that is what the author asked for; pretending they are private bookkeeping is not. Nothing ever reads the ledger from here.
tidy._depot_comment: Depot exports get their own target — they are holdings, not receipts, and the briefing reads them. The broker calls the file 'investments.csv', which no receipt pattern would ever have caught; it would have ended up in the holding pen and nothing would have said so.

models._comment: Not yet measured for this domain — these are the starting points, and make finance-eval replaces them with numbers. 190 bookings a month make small the obvious first try: the cost question does not exist at that volume, so what gets measured is accuracy and consistency, not price.

agent._comment: IDs are written back by agents/sync.py. Do not edit by hand.

limits._comment: The first full run over 649 bookings died on HTTP 429 (token rate limit) after 23, at concurrency 10 with no pause. The limit counts TOKENS per minute, not requests, so more waiting is the only remedy: 6 at a time, 40 per chunk, 8 seconds between chunks, plus exponential backoff per booking. Slower than the inbox domain because a booking prompt is longer than an email envelope.

measurement._comment: Filled by make finance-eval and by the first real runs. Numbers live next to the setting they justify (repo rule 6).
